description: Supplementary knowledge related to water licence application drawings, including practical guidance on drawing quality and completeness, common issues that may affect review, general definitions of image file formats, and guidance for accessing current drawing standards.

knowledge_items.title: Drawing Quality and Completeness
keywords: can I draw in a napkin
knowledge_items.content: Drawings are a key source of information for reviewers and are often relied on to understand how water is diverted, conveyed, and used, especially where form fields do not capture sufficient detail ('A picture is worth a thousand words'). Avoid common issues such as: informal or incomplete drawings (e.g., 'back-of-the-napkin'), incorrectly located features (e.g., wrong point of diversion), and missing parts of the system between the source and end use. These issues frequently result in follow-up or clarification before review can proceed.

knowledge_items.title: What is JPEG?
knowledge_items.content: JPEG is a widely used image format for compressing photos, and images can also be stored in other formats such as PNG, GIF, or WebP depending on how they need to be used.

knowledge_items.title: Latest Application Drawing Standards
